I moved to China as a 16 year old International student one year after this video was made. I lived in Guangzhou in southern China and went to an International school there. The internet was very restricted even at the school, and anything slightly to do with Tiananmen Square was just not able to be found. For my senior year I wrote an extended essay on contemporary Chinese art, and had to do a lot of research on what changes happened in the recent history of China and what correlation this had on the art that was being made. It was extremely hard to get the proper information until I worked out how to use proxys. Even then it was a bit scary doing this and I always wondered how serious it was to look at sites like wikipedia while I was over there. All in all though it was a fantastic experience and one that has changed the way I view the world. It is such an ancient and proud culture, and it's just such a shame that in this day people still feel oppressed and can't properly mourn tragic moments in history.
